faq: Which tools do you use for feedback?

Whatever is simple and cheap for you, such as a form in your app saving to Airtable or Google Sheets, or a tool like Canny. We avoid heavy paid tools unless you ask. The cost, if any, is billed to you.
Can you contact my users for interviews?
We can write the invitation for you to send. We only contact people who have signed up for your product and agreed to hear from you, and we do not scrape emails or message strangers.
How many replies do I need for this to be useful?
Even 15 to 30 honest replies show clear patterns in an early product. We tell you in the summary how confident the patterns are and where you need more voices before deciding.
Will the feedback form slow down my product?
No. It is a small piece of code that loads after the page is ready. We test page speed before and after, and remove it if it ever gets in the way of the main flow.

desc:
A user feedback system for early SaaS products collects what your first users think and turns it into a ranked list of changes. Ecom Swift LLC adds the forms and surveys to your product, organizes the replies and shows you what to fix first.

## What is a feedback loop for a SaaS product?

A feedback loop is a repeatable way to gather opinions from users, sort them and act on them. It has four parts: a place for users to speak, a place where replies land, a method for grouping them and a decision about what to build.

Without all four, feedback becomes a pile of scattered messages in email, chat and memory. With them, you can see patterns instead of reacting to whoever wrote last.

## Why early users rarely tell you what is wrong

Most people who dislike a product simply leave. They do not write a message, because it takes effort and they do not expect anything to change. The founder sees fewer logins and has to guess why. Those who do write often describe a solution, such as a new button, rather than the problem behind it.

Making feedback easy and asking at the right moments changes this. A one-click form inside the product catches the thought while it is fresh. An exit survey reaches the people who would otherwise vanish silently, and they are the ones who know best what is broken.

## How structured feedback improves what you build

Feedback matters because it replaces opinion with evidence. Three users asking for the same thing is a signal; one loud request is not. Tagging replies as bugs, ideas and questions separates what must be repaired from what might be added. Ranking the themes shows you whether to polish the first workflow or build a second one.

It also protects your time. Teams without a loop tend to build whatever the most recent conversation suggested. A ranked list gives you a reason to say no, and a record you can show to partners or backers.

## What a working feedback system includes

- A feedback button or form inside the product, reachable from every main screen.
- A thank-you message so people know their reply arrived.
- One shared inbox, sheet or board where every reply is stored.
- Tags that separate bugs, ideas and questions.
- A short welcome survey that asks why the person signed up.
- An exit survey that asks why a person is leaving.
- An interview script with neutral questions that avoid leading the answer.
- Optional public request board where users vote on ideas.
- A written summary that groups replies into themes.
- A ranked list of what to build or fix next.

## What we do

We choose a lightweight tool that fits your stack and place a form or widget in your product. Replies flow into a sheet or board you own, with tags applied. We then write the surveys, keeping the questions short and specific so people actually finish them.

The Basic package sets up the form, the inbox, a thank-you message and a short reading guide. Standard adds welcome and exit surveys, tags and a summary of the first batch of replies. Premium adds an interview script, a small number of interviews run and written up, an optional public request board and a ranked list of next steps. Extra interviews and survey types are available as add-ons.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Ask about the problem users are trying to solve, not only about features.
- Read every reply during the first weeks.
- Reply to people who wrote in, even with a short note.
- Group feedback by theme before deciding anything.
- Share what you changed, so users see that writing in works.

**Avoid:**
- Asking long surveys with many required fields.
- Treating a single request as a market trend.
- Leading questions such as "Would you love a dark mode?"
- Promising features to users while you gather ideas.
- Leaving replies in several places that nobody checks.

## Who this service is for

Founders who launched quietly and are unsure why users are not returning will find the exit survey especially useful. Teams with a small private beta can use the interview script to learn from the first few customers. Product owners who already receive scattered messages benefit from one organized inbox and a clear ranking.

## What we need from you

Access to your product code or admin area as a collaborator, a list of your current users or beta group if you want interviews, and a sentence on what you most want to learn. We never need passwords. For interviews, you introduce us to willing users, and we handle the questions and notes.
